howto_md:
## How to use this booklet

This booklet is a map of the world's sports and games. Every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what the sport or game is, where it began, who governs it and where it is popular. Every entry has an ID (such as SPT-03.1 for cricket) that is also its address on the website.

- **Parts** are the big branches (outdoor, indoor, mind games, digital, folk, parasports, history, events, awards...).
- **Sections (SPT-01, SPT-02...)** are the main topics; each opens with a *Before you start* box.
- **Sub-sections and entries** carry a ☐ box: tick it when you have played, watched or explored it.
- **Registers** list 30 landmark sports, the year-wise timeline and 14 world events with first and latest winners (checked 3 November 2026).
- **Tags** (#cricket #kabaddi #olympics) and **See also** links connect related pages.
- Start with **Part 0**, seven two-minute questions about why we play.
howto_intro: This booklet is a map of the world's sports and games: outdoor and indoor sports, mind games, video games and esports, traditional games of India and the world, parasports, history, events, awards, legends, science, ideas and a practical guide. Every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what the thing is and why it matters.
Every entry has an ID (such as SPT-03.1 for cricket). The same ID is the entry's address on curioussparoows.com, where each one is growing into its own page.
howto_boxes: **Parts:** the intro questions, the master map, outdoor and indoor sports, mind games, digital games, folk games, parasports, history, events, awards, people, science, ideas, the practical guide, reviews, navigation and sources.
**Sections (SPT-01 to SPT-34):** the main topics, each opening with a *Before you start* box.
**Sub-sections and entries (☐):** one or two lines each; tick the box when you have played or watched.
**Registers:** 30 sports, the timeline and 14 world events. They are a sourced selection; the full lists grow on the website.
**Step 2.** Find your favourite sport in the master map (Part 1).
**Step 3.** Visit the folk games of your own state in Part 6.
**Step 4.** Follow tags and See also links to films, books, music and technology.
**Step 5.** Tick ☐ as you play or watch, and use the tracker at the end.

Knowledge belongs to the people who created it. Every fact here stands on a source listed in Part 17, and every "latest" fact says when it was checked. Where something could not be verified, we say so instead of guessing. Found a mistake? Tell us, and we will fix it and thank you.
